name: Simultaneous Extensions Grouped by Acquired Support
statement: Let nonempty ample $S\subseteq Q_F$ and let $U\subseteq Q_F\setminus S$ be finitely many tips such that every one-tip extension $S\cup\{a\}$ is ample, with acquired support $I_a$. For each occurring support $I$, put $U_I=\{a:I_a=I\}$ and $R_I=\{a|_{F\setminus I}:a\in U_I\}$, and let $X=S\cup U$. Then $X$ is ample exactly when every row $R_I$ is ample. Under these conditions, $X^I=R_I$ and $\operatorname{Sh}(X)=\operatorname{Sh}(S)\dot\cup\dot\bigcup_I\{I\cup J:J\in\operatorname{Sh}(R_I)\}$. Moreover, $X$ peels to $S$ exactly when every row $R_I$ is dismantlable ample. The empty tip set is allowed.
proof: All tips in one group realize the unique trace of $I$ missing from $S$, and no tip from another group can realize that trace without acquiring $I$ as a second support. Thus the full $I$-fibres of $X$ occur exactly over $R_I$, proving $X^I=R_I$ and necessity by reduction closure. Conversely, each cube in $R_I$ lifts through the punctured $I$-fibres in $S$ to a full cube on $I$ together with its row support. Contributions from distinct acquired supports cannot contain one another and are disjoint. If all rows are ample, their shadow sizes sum with $|S|$ to $|X|$, so Sandwich equality proves ampleness and the exact shadow. A tip is a corner exactly when its row projection is a corner, even after arbitrary other tips have been deleted. Row peelings therefore lift and concatenate to a peeling down to $S$, while any relative peeling projects to complete peelings of every row.
